assets/vo/s01-094cf9e1.mp3: Here's how to use Opus five point five as your daily driver, in under sixty seconds.
assets/vo/s01-e18e5d29.mp3: Say growth slowed at your retail company, and your manager has four theories to test.
assets/vo/s02-f9522f44.mp3: Habit one: put everything in your first message. Say what the goal is, what the finished output looks like, and when to stop and ask.
assets/vo/s03-05252774.mp3: Habit two: drop "think hard." Thinking is always on, and removing the phrase made replies start sooner, with no clear drop in quality.
assets/vo/s04-bbcccff6.mp3: Habit three: leave effort on Medium, the default. In testing, Medium matched or beat Opus five at High, so move up only when Medium stalls.
assets/vo/s05-8dea5b47.mp3: Habit four: ask for the finished file, not an outline.
assets/vo/s06-ec4fed0c.mp3: Claude tested all four theories against your sales data, and none held up, though one couldn't be fully ruled out.
assets/vo/s06-9501af69.mp3: It also found what nobody had raised. New stores opened too close to old ones and pulled sales away.
